title: tenant-buffer-pool-rebalancer-and-utilization-signal-mediator
author: Asha Patel
release_notes: Adds a new tenant buffer pool rebalancer that reduces oscillation when tenants compete for reserved capacity; exposes utilization damping metrics and a fairness gate configurable via Dedicated feature flag.
description: Motivation: tenants with bursty traffic were observed to induce oscillatory reassignments of reserved buffer credits during contention windows which degraded P99 latency for mid-tier customers. This PR introduces a conservative, proportional rebalancer for tenant buffer pools combined with a utilization-signal mediation layer that smooths short-term noise and applies a fairness gate to protect latency-sensitive SLOs. The change is opt-in behind a feature flag and includes backward-compatible fallbacks to the existing allocation ledger. Implementation summary: 1) controller: tenant_buffer_rebalancer - samples per-tenant occupancy and in-flight rates, computes target deltas using a damped proportional allocator, and emits reassignments via the existing reservation API; 2) util-signal-mediator: lightweight EWMA smoothing with configurable half-life and an outlier clamp that prevents a single spike from triggering rebalances; 3) fairness gate: when a tenant's latency SLO metric cross-check fails, rebalancer reduces reclamation aggressiveness for that tenant; 4) telemetry: new prometheus metrics (rb_rebalance_attempts_total, rb_rebalance_succeeded_total, rb_util_ewma, rb_fairness_skips_total) and structured tracing spans to link rebalances to tenant traces; 5) migration: small idempotent background job to reconcile existing reservation ledgers to the new buffer accounting (no data loss). The description below enumerates commits, changed paths, CI results, and the review thread. This PR is targeted to Dedicated capacity and fleet management improvements and aims to decrease P99 tail latency regressions under multi-tenant contention while keeping burst capacity utilization high.

ci_checks: Presubmit: lint (initially failed, fixed), unit-tests (all pass), integration-e2e (flaky on first run due to harness timeout, retried and passed), security-scan (no findings), chart-lint (pass). Final CI state: pass.
observability_changes: Adds new Prometheus counters/gauges and tracing spans. Updated the console dashboard JSON to include a rebalancer panel and P99 guardrail alerts; operator docs include suggested alert thresholds.
performance_note: Benchmarking on a 40-tenant synthetic workload showed a 22% reduction in median rebalancer-induced churn and a 12% improvement in 99th-percentile latency for medium-tier tenants under sustained contention; warmup costs are minor due to damped deltas.
migration_plan: Idempotent reconcile_buffer_ledgers job runs with a dry-run mode; operators should run dry-run during maintenance window and then switch to apply mode. Backwards compatibility preserved; there is a feature flag to disable the rebalancer if unexpected behavior occurs.
operator_docs: docs/operator/tenant-buffer-rebalancer.md explains feature flag, tuning knobs (ewma_half_life_seconds, clamp_window_seconds, max_reassign_pct), and migration steps with examples.
merge_outcome: Squash and merge to main. Merge commit message: 'tenant buffer pool rebalancer + util-signal mediator (ENG-3174): introduce damped proportional reserve rebalancer, EWMA util smoothing, fairness gate, metrics, and migration job.'
post_merge_actions: Deployed to staging behind feature flag on 2025-01-23; scheduled progressive ramp to production with canary pool on 2025-01-28. Ops runbook entry created referencing SUP-4421.
notes: This PR is intentionally conservative: rebalancer only reassigns from warm spare pools first and never reduces hard reservation guarantees below safety floor. Future follow-ups planned for fine-grained per-tenant half-life autotuning and cross-cluster spillover policies.
